🔊 Iranian nation remains strong to overcome challenges: Administration spokesperson

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Administration spokesperson Fatemeh Mohajerani, referring to the devastation caused by the renewed US war of aggression against Iran, has said that the resilient Iranian nation remains steadfast in the face of external threats and will overcome these difficult times.

In a press briefing in Tehran on Tuesday, Mohajerani addressed a number of issues related to national, regional, and international developments, including repeated US attacks on civilian and vital public infrastructure in southern parts of the country.
​
Stating that the damage to people’s property has been extensive, she pointed to attacks on fishing and tourism boats that are the only source of livelihood for a large number of people along Iran’s southern coast.
​
The spokesperson referred to attacks on the Chabahar Naval Traffic Control Tower, the Bushehr Meteorological Center and Bushehr Airport, the Bandar Abbas branch railway, and aviation facilities, saying the aggressive enemy had targeted facilities that were used purely for public and civil services.
​
She also pointed to a report by the Ministry of Roads and Urban Development on damage to 12 bridges and two tunnels, as well as the round-the-clock efforts of road workers to provide alternative routes for commuters and transportation.
​
Despite all the damage and difficulties caused by the enemy, Mohajerani praised the Iranian people, particularly those living in coastal and border regions, for their patience, resistance, and resilience, stressing that the nation would overcome these difficult times with the same wisdom and prudence.
​
She also expressed gratitude to the Iranian Armed Forces, including generals, admirals, and commanders, for their steadfastness and vigilance in high and sweltering temperatures to safeguard Iran’s sovereignty, independence, and territorial integrity.

A UK criminal gang has been sentenced after stealing over £4 million ($5.4M) in cryptocurrency from eight victims by posing as police officers.

The group used convincing fake police websites to deceive targets into handing over their crypto holdings. The fraud involved direct impersonation of law enforcement, a tactic designed to pressure victims into compliance under the guise of official investigations.

The case highlights the growing use of authority impersonation in crypto-related fraud, where fake government and law enforcement identities are deployed to bypass victims' skepticism.
